Write the overall analysis to a local markdown file referencing both SVGs via standard `![<title>](<name>.svg)` image syntax — NOT a ```mermaid fenced code block, the final PDF renderer can only show an embedded image, not Mermaid source — then upload it to MinIO (this is the plan_release <-> kickoff hand-off store, not a GitLab wiki): `mc alias set local $MINIO_ENDPOINT $MINIO_ROOT_USER $MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD >/dev/null && mc cp <your-file>.md local/release-reports/{{ $node['Webhook Trigger'].json.body.body.version }}/architecture.md`. Then, for EVERY new service (not existing/changed-only services) identified above, write a SEPARATE local markdown file containing only that service's own sequence diagram for its primary flow, its own flowchart for its main decision/process logic, an ERD (`erDiagram`) if it owns persistence (omit and say so if it doesn't) — each rendered to its own SVG via `render-mermaid.sh` the same way and referenced via `![](...)` image syntax, never a raw ```mermaid fence — and an API doc table (columns Method, Path, Request, Response, Auth) listing every endpoint it exposes — one markdown file per service, never combined — and upload each (markdown AND its SVGs) as its own object(s): `mc cp <service-file>.md local/release-reports/{{ $node['Webhook Trigger'].json.body.body.version }}/architecture-<service-slug>.md` (service-slug = the service name, lowercased, spaces to hyphens), SVGs alongside it the same way. Report the exact object path of the overall file, every per-service file, and every SVG once all uploads succeed.

assignments.value: =Reporting only — do NOT create any Taiga tickets or GitLab branches here, this is a planning-stage estimate, kickoff (which does create the real tickets/branches) hasn't run yet, and do NOT touch GitLab or Taiga at all (no wiki reads/writes) — fetch the PRD and Architecture sections from MinIO instead of GitLab: `mc alias set local $MINIO_ENDPOINT $MINIO_ROOT_USER $MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD >/dev/null && mc cat local/release-reports/{{ $node['Webhook Trigger'].json.body.body.version }}/prd.md` and `mc cat local/release-reports/{{ $node['Webhook Trigger'].json.body.body.version }}/architecture.md` for the story list and technical scope. For EACH story, break it into task-level items by role x feature — NOT one generic task per story — the same decomposition a Tech Lead would use at kickoff: identify the distinct backend/frontend/api features the story touches (e.g. a login story might be 'frontend: login page' + 'backend: login mechanism' + 'api: login endpoint contract'). For each task, estimate development time in hours, accounting for the risk/complexity surfaced in the Architecture section and QA/Security gate outputs above (a task touching a flagged risk area should carry a wider/higher estimate, say so). Skip any role a story genuinely doesn't touch. Produce a markdown table per story: columns Task (role-prefixed, e.g. '[backend] login mechanism'), Estimated Hours, Notes (assumptions/risk driving the number) — plus a per-story subtotal row and a grand total at the end for the whole release. Write this to a local markdown file, then upload it to MinIO: `mc cp <your-file>.md local/release-reports/{{ $node['Webhook Trigger'].json.body.body.version }}/estimate.md`. Report the exact object path once the upload succeeds.

=Report compiler — planning stage only, do NOT touch GitLab or Taiga. `mc alias set local $MINIO_ENDPOINT $MINIO_ROOT_USER $MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD >/dev/null`, then download EVERYTHING uploaded for {{ $node['Webhook Trigger'].json.body.body.version }} in one shot (markdown sections AND every diagram SVG they reference): `mc cp --recursive local/release-reports/{{ $node['Webhook Trigger'].json.body.body.version }}/ .` — architecture.md/schema-impact.md/qa-risk.md/security-threat.md/ux-review.md/prd.md/estimate.md and their SVGs land in the current directory together, so the markdown's `![](<name>.svg)` references resolve as relative paths once you assemble combined.md here. Some sections may be missing if an earlier step failed; skip missing ones and note the gap, don't fail the whole compile over it.

Assemble combined.md as a fixed proposal template — these 20 sections, in this exact order, each its own `# <N>. <Section>` markdown heading (source material in brackets; where no generated section maps to it, write the standard short paragraph given, don't leave it blank or invent unsupported specifics):
1. Cover Page — project name, version, revision, today's date (from the webhook vars, no source file needed).
2. Table of Contents — omit the content, `publish-pdf.sh`'s pandoc call renders this automatically from headings via --toc.
3. Executive Summary — 2-3 sentences synthesized from prd.md's own opening/goal, not copied verbatim.
4. Project Objectives — extract the measurable goals/KPIs from prd.md.
5. Scope of Work — extract in-scope features by user type and any explicit out-of-scope items from prd.md.
6. Technical Approach / Solution Architecture — architecture.md in full, including its diagram image references as-is (these are real rendered vector SVGs, not Mermaid source — see `publish-pdf.sh` invocation below for how they get bundled into the PDF).
7. Technology Stack — pull the stack choices already stated in architecture.md into a short table (frontend/backend/database/hosting/CI-CD); if architecture.md doesn't break it out this cleanly, say so and give the best table extractable from it rather than fabricating entries.
8. Non-Functional Requirements — performance/scalability/security/availability points pulled from architecture.md and security-threat.md.
9. Team Composition & Roles — static: list the SDLC roles this pipeline runs (Architect, Data Engineer, PM, Tech Lead, Backend/Frontend Developer, QA, Security, DevOps, UX, Product Owner, Release Manager) with a one-line responsibility each; this is a fixed pipeline roster, not a staffing plan.
10. Project Timeline/Milestones — the phase breakdown and durations from estimate.md.
11. Deliverables — the concrete outputs listed in estimate.md and prd.md (source code, docs, deployed services).
12. Assumptions & Dependencies — any cross-story/external dependency noted in prd.md; if none, write "No external dependencies identified at planning time."
13. Risk Analysis & Mitigation Plan — qa-risk.md and security-threat.md combined, each risk with impact/likelihood/mitigation as those reports already structure it.
14. Change Management Process — static boilerplate: "Scope changes are raised as new Taiga stories against this release's epic and re-estimated by Tech Lead; they do not retroactively alter this proposal."
15. Communication & Reporting Plan — static boilerplate: "This is an automated SDLC pipeline (n8n-orchestrated agent pods) — there are no standing meetings; progress is tracked live in Taiga, and sign-off gates notify via the project's configured channel."
16. Testing & Quality Assurance — qa-risk.md's testing approach and acceptance criteria.
17. Deployment & Release Strategy — derived from architecture.md's deployment section plus the pipeline's own SIT -> UAT -> staging -> production flow (ArgoCD-managed, ArgoCD Image Updater promotes tags).
18. Maintenance & Support Plan — static boilerplate: "Post-release monitoring runs through the shared Grafana/Loki/Tempo stack; see F-21/F-22's rollback flow for incident response."
19. Cost Estimate/Pricing — estimate.md's effort breakdown (this homelab pipeline has no $ pricing — present it as effort/time, not currency).
20. Appendices — ux-review.md in full, plus schema-impact.md if it wasn't already folded into section 8.

Then run: `publish-pdf.sh {{ $node['Webhook Trigger'].json.body.body.project }} {{ $node['Webhook Trigger'].json.body.body.version }} {{ $node['Webhook Trigger'].json.body.body.revision ?? '1' }} combined.md *.svg` — this is a pre-built script already on this image, it converts combined.md to PDF in a throwaway Kubernetes Job (pandoc lives there, not on this always-resident pod), bundling every trailing SVG argument alongside it so pandoc can resolve combined.md's image references, and uploads the PDF to Nextcloud, then cleans the Job up itself. It prints the uploaded path on success, or a Job failure/timeout message plus the pandoc/upload container logs on stderr on failure — do not try to reimplement any of this yourself, just run the script (with every downloaded `.svg` passed after combined.md) and report exactly what it printed.
